chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure.'
He said: When the servant commits a felony in other than the Haram, then he flees into the Haram, there is no leeway for anyone to seize him inside the Haram.
But he is prevented from the market, and he is neither sold to nor fed, nor given drink, nor spoken to. For when that is done with him, he would desire to come out, and he would be seized.
And when he commits a crime inside the Haram with a felony, the Legal Punishment (Hadd) is established upon him inside the Haram, because he did not leave for the Haram its Sanctity.

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca or Masjid al-Haram)
key_terms.يُبَايَعُ: He is sold/traded (in the market context)

ai.seo_question: How is a criminal treated if they flee into the Haram versus if they commit the crime inside it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuance of 'aman' (security) in the Haram, distinguishing between physical immunity from immediate arrest and the preservation of sanctity. It establishes that while a fugitive is protected from being dragged out, social exclusion serves as a psychological pressure to exit, whereas those who violate the Haram's sanctity within its bounds face immediate Hadd punishment, reflecting the principle that the sanctuary's honor is not a shield for its desecration.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:97] and whoever enters it shall be secure.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the servant commits a felony in other than the Al-Harram, then he flees into the Al-Harram, there is no leeway for anyone that he seizes him inside the Al-Harram.
But he can be prevented from the market, and he can neither sell, nor feed, nor drink, nor speak (to anyone). So when that is done with him, he would desire to come out, and he would be seized.

And when he commits a crime inside the Al-Harram with a felony, the Legal Punishment (Hadd) would be established upon him inside the Al-Harram, because he did not leave for the Al-Harram, its Sanctity’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘Whoever enters it (al-Haram, the sacred area) gains immunity. 5 [3:96]
He (the Imam) said, ‘If a servant (of Allah) commits a crime outside al-Haram (the sacred area) then flees to al- Haram, no one can arrest him inside al-Haram;
however, he can be stopped from entering the market place, to buy or sell; he is not fed, provided drink or spoken to. If this is done, he eventually leaves; then he can be arrested.
If one commits a crime inside al-Haram, he is brought to justice inside al- Haram;
he has violated the sanctity of al-Haram.’”
